summary.text: Alex Vangalen is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Benambra at the 2026 Victorian election. He has lived around Wodonga for about 30 years and works as a behaviour support practitioner with people with disability, and he belongs to the Australian Services Union. He holds degrees in psychological science and pharmacy.

priorities.text: More public investment in transport, health care and public housing in Benambra
Tackling housing shortages and the cost of living
We need public services that prioritise people, not the pockets of big business.

sources.title: Benambra: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Alex Vangalen, Victorian Socialists

summary.text: Evette Pepper is the Family First candidate for Benambra at the 2026 Victorian election. She has three children and nine grandchildren, brought up her family as a single mother while juggling part-time work and home businesses, and later gained counselling qualifications. She has helped with bushfire recovery in the Upper Murray, has led HART Ministry International's Australian arm since 2023, and became an ordained pastor in 2024.

occupation.text: Pastor and ministry leader; trained counsellor

prior_roles.role: CEO and board member, HMI International
Set up a community art group, studio and exhibition space after the 2020 Upper Murray bushfires
prior_roles.organisation: Towong Shire Council (Working for Victoria grant)

prior_roles.note: The party page says she joined the team as a volunteer in 2021 and helped again during the 2026 fires.

priorities.text: Bringing down living costs, including rent, taxes, fuel and power bills
Keeping Australia's resources for Australians rather than selling them overseas
Favouring productive farmland over badly planned renewable energy projects
Proper funding for local health services and roads
Defending free speech and religious freedom, and opposing abortion

sources.title: Benambra: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Evette Pepper, Candidate for Benambra, Family First

summary.text: Graham Parton is the Greens candidate for Benambra at the 2026 Victorian election. He spent his working life in human resources and environmental management, and since retiring has been writing biographies of local people and guiding tours at the Old Beechworth Gaol. He ran for Indigo Shire Council as a Greens candidate in 2024 and was not elected.

occupation.text: Retired; formerly human resources and environmental management

priorities.text: Benambra deserves a representative who listens, acts with compassion, and plans for the future
Serious action on climate change and its effects on farmers and regional towns
Turning down donations from wealthy individuals and large industries
Better health care, protection of biodiversity and more resilient country communities

summary.text: Kellie Sheppard is the One Nation candidate for Benambra at the 2026 Victorian election. According to the ABC, she owns a small business and a hobby farm, and has previously worked as a writer and journalist and led a national health charity as its director. One Nation's candidate page could not be read for this profile.

sources.title: Benambra: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Dr Lachie McKeeman is a general practitioner in Wodonga and an independent candidate for Benambra at the 2026 Victorian election, backed by the Community for Benambra group. Based in the state's north-east since 2013, he volunteers with the CFA brigade at Wooragee and has campaigned publicly for a new Albury-Wodonga hospital.

prior_roles.note: His campaign site lists this as a current role; the ABC describes him as a former secretary.

priorities.text: Securing a greenfield hospital and expanding our workforce.
Safe roads should be a basic standard, not an election promise.
Make it easier to build homes in regional Victoria.
Getting big money out of politics and stronger integrity in government
Keeping Wodonga Golf Course as green space

summary.text: Mike Fuery is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Benambra at the 2026 Victorian election. He was a paramedic for 40 years, based in Wodonga from 1995, and retired in 2023. He also stood for the party in Benambra in 2022, when he received 2.8% of the primary vote.

priorities.text: Prevention-first health policy, through education and a healthier food system
Tackling the links between animal farming, diseases that jump from animals and antibiotic resistance
Reducing farming's environmental impact to help on climate and protect native species
Non-lethal ways for people and wildlife to coexist
More support for local animal rescuers and sanctuaries

summary.text: Steve Martin is the Liberal candidate for Benambra at the 2026 Victorian election. An engineer who studied at the University of New South Wales and La Trobe University, he is an engineering manager with the Nordcon land development firm and lives in Wodonga. He was the Liberal candidate for the federal seat of Indi in 2019, which the independent Helen Haines won.

priorities.text: More beds and expanded health services in the Albury Wodonga Health redevelopment
Saving Wodonga Golf Course
Upgrading local roads
Lower housing taxes so local families can buy or build a first home

summary.text: Tim Quilty is the Libertarian candidate for Benambra at the 2026 Victorian election. An accountant and former farmer, he sat in the Legislative Council for Northern Victoria Region from 2018 to 2022 for the Liberal Democrats (since renamed the Libertarians), losing his seat in 2022. Before that he was a City of Wodonga councillor, and he has lived in Wodonga since 2011.
